business_scope.primary_industry_name: Proprietary Ultra-Low Latency Algorithmic Market Making

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (comprehensive DTA, in force)
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations) regional free trade agreement
OECD-standard Tax Information Exchange Agreement network administered by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 (No. 18 of 2018); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2011 (No. 28 of 2011); International Companies Act 1987, as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2018; International Companies (Register of Beneficial Owners) Regulations 2019; supervised by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and the Registrar of International Companies under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. The beneficial-ownership register must be established and maintained by a licensed registered agent at the company's registered office in Samoa and is accessible to the Registrar, the FIU, and law-enforcement authorities on request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport and proof of residential address of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public licensed in the country of origin of the signatory, or a notary public licensed in Samoa if executed domestically
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — Samoa is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; authentication is effected by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the nearest accredited Samoan diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction companies registry or competent corporate registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Samoan diplomatic mission having consular competence over the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and prime-brokerage KYC attestation for the proposed proprietary high-frequency trading accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed prime brokerage counterparty in the clearing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization, or certified true copy countersigned by the licensed Samoan registered agent where the registry accepts a certified-copy alternative

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 and Samoa FIU directives: (i) PEP screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against domestic PEP lists, international publicly available PEP databases, and commercially licensed PEP screeners; (ii) sanctions screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and other OFAC-administered sanctions lists, EU and UK sanctions lists, and the domestic designations list maintained by the Samoa FIU; (iii) negative-news and watch-list vetting of all natural persons and corporate entities in the ownership chain. Screening must be completed prior to incorporation, repeated immediately prior to each high-risk wire or clearing payment, and performed on a rolling basis for ultra-low-latency algorithmic market-making activity. Any match or suspicious occurrence must be escalated to the Samoa FIU under statutory suspicious-transaction reporting timeframes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Registrar of International Companies — Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; name-clearance submissions are transmitted exclusively through SRO-licensed registered agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Section 10 of the International Companies Act 1987 requires a distinct corporate name expressed in Latin (Roman) script. Samoan and English names are acceptable; names derived from non-Latin scripts must be accompanied by an English transliteration and may not be reserved in script form alone. The name must not be misleading as to the company's regulated financial-object character, must contain an approved corporate designator (Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Société Anonyme, or an approved abbreviation) as its last word or element, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any reserved or registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a written name-rejection notice issued by the Registrar of International Companies, the applicant, acting through its licensed registered agent, may: (i) within 14 days of rejection, lodge a formal written appeal with the Registrar together with the rejection notice, a new Name Clearance Request, and the applicable reappraisal fee; (ii) if refused, petition the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for administrative review within 30 days of the Registrar's decision; and (iii) if administrative review is unsuccessful, seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance and general administrative-law principles. An identical rejected name may not be re-submitted; a modified or transliterated alternative may be filed without prejudice. A reservation that expires after the 30-day window is released to the public name pool and requires a fresh filing, but the Registrar may, on good cause shown by the registered agent, grant a single extension of up to an additional 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible. Section 107 of the International Companies Act 1987 requires a physical registered office in Samoa maintained by a licensed registered agent, staffed during business hours and capable of receiving legal process and official notices. A virtual-office address in lieu of the agent's physical premises does not satisfy the statutory mandate; however, back-office administrative functions may be performed remotely and the low-latency trading infrastructure may be hosted outside Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a non-licensed offshore proprietary trading vehicle in the first operational year, approximately 5-10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection under the Samoa FIU risk-based supervisory framework; the probability increases to 15-25% where UBO register deficiencies, PEP flags, or suspicious Fedwire clearing activity trigger a targeted compliance visit under the Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2011.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-filing advisory on statutory licensing pre-clearance for proprietary high-frequency trading and financial-services characterization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2001 (Samoa), ss 5-6 (Incorporation Procedure), s 17 (Memorandum of Association), s 19 (Articles of Association), s 18 (Registered Office); International Companies Act regime consolidated under the Companies Act 2001
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form 01 Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed; issued capital may be expressed in any freely convertible currency, and no escrow or capital deposit account requirement is enforced by the Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscription of 1,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each by the sole subscriber is accepted; the shares are allotted and issued fully paid, and entry in the register of members is approved. RESOLVED THAT the registered office situated at Level 1, Leeward Building, Apia, Samoa, is adopted and filed with the Registrar of Companies. RESOLVED THAT Mr. John Faletoese is appointed Resident Director, Ms. Lana Tuilaepa as Company Secretary, and Mr. Samuel Leavasa as Chief Executive Officer, each serving until removed. RESOLVED THAT the Resident Agent is retained pursuant to the Companies Act 2001, and the directors are authorized to execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association and file all incorporation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, MCIL, Apia (online name search portal or physical registry counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the preferred corporate name for a name search against the Registry's database; specify proposed activity as proprietary algorithmic trading; pay the name reservation fee; the name is reserved for 30 days pending submission of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Certified copy of incorporator's passport or beneficial owner identification
Name search and reservation fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or identical to an existing entity, file a first alternative name within 5 business days or request written reasons and administrative review by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Resident Agent under MCIL authority, with notarization before a Samoan Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the Resident Agent to prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the Companies Act 2001; the sole subscriber executes the documents before a Notary Public in Samoa; arrange apostille certification where the documents will be filed with foreign clearing houses or prime brokers.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Draft Articles of Association
Subscriber's notarized signature page and identity evidence
Consents to act of proposed directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry defects the documents for drafting errors, amend the relevant clauses and re-execute the corrected pages before the notary; no additional government fee applies for rectification within the original submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Statutory Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form 01 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the statutory declaration of compliance executed by the Resident Agent, and evidence of payment of the US$100 government incorporation fee; confirm the registered office address and the identity particulars of directors, secretary, and shareholder in the application.
required_dossiers: Form 01 Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory declaration of compliance by the Resident Agent
Government fee payment receipt
Beneficial ownership and director identity dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registry requisition letter within 14 days; supply supplementary evidence of identity or corrected documents; failure to cure within 14 days necessitates re-filing under a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and enters the company in the International Companies Register; review the certificate for exact name, date, company number, and liability limitation wording before acceptance.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application bundle
Certified copy of subscriber's consent to incorporation
Registered office confirmation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error in name or date, apply formally for rectification and a corrected certificate; the Registrar issues a corrective instrument without loss of original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Resident Agent Appointment Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL Licensed Resident Agent and Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of appointment of the Resident Agent together with the registered office consent form and officer consent forms; open the statutory registers including register of members, register of directors, and register of charges; ensure the registered office is physically accessible in Apia during business hours.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent form from the office landlord
Resident Agent acceptance letter
Officer consent and appointment forms
Opening pages of the statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the appointment notice for incomplete consents, resubmit with properly witnessed signatures; late filing penalties are mitigated by making a voluntary declaration and the remedial filing within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Formalities, Share Certificates, and KYC/AML File
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent and Company Compliance Officer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue share certificates to the subscriber, execute the company seal if desired, maintain the minute book, prepare the beneficial ownership register, and complete the customer due diligence file for the proprietary trader and ultimate beneficial owners; obtain written confirmation of the company's low-risk AML classification for the algorithmic market-making business model.
required_dossiers: Share certificates
Register of members and beneficial owners
First board resolution minutes
AML/CFT customer due diligence and risk assessment pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML file is queried by the Resident Agent's compliance officer, supplement the source of funds and corporate ownership documentation; any register correction is effected by board resolution and a corrective filing with the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Industrial and Business Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Incorporation of an International Company (Offshore Proprietary Trading Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Division of Environment and Conservation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category III (No full EIA Report required; purely financial algorithm trading has no land disturbance, construction, or stationary emission source)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge generated by core trading activity; office premises must comply with sanitary wastewater limits under the Water Resources Management Act; any backup generator must not emit visible smoke beyond 5% opacity and must be serviced to manufacturer's air quality standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority confirming compliance for the occupied office floor; structural load inspection for server racks and trading infrastructure by a licensed civil engineer; Occupational Safety and Health worksite clearance from MCIL covering electrical safety, emergency exits, and workstation ergonomics

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Samoa (successor to the Samoa Tax and Customs Administration); official government tax portal and e-services: www.samoagovt.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident-owned proprietary high-frequency trading vehicle is incorporated as an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 via the Samoa International Companies Registry (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour). The Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation containing the IC registration number; because the IC automatically holds statutory tax-exempt status, no income tax TIN is issued. If the IC ever undertakes non-exempt domestic taxable supplies or elects to become taxable, it must file the MfR application for a Tax Identification Number and VAGST registration under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003, supported by the certificate of incorporation, registered agent details and a written description of trading activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An International Company may elect under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 1997 to become a taxable company by filing written notice with the Ministry for Revenue, thereby exiting the automatic exemption from income tax, VAGST and stamp duty. Samoa has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elective regime; entity classification is determined statutorily by the International Companies Act and administratively by the Commissioner of the Ministry for Revenue, with no OECD hybrid branch elections available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 200,000 (Samoa Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; tax-exempt International Companies are outside the VAGST net and may not register unless they validly revoke their exempt status
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance API, or digital stamping mandate exists in Samoa; registered persons must issue compliant VAGST invoices, maintain records for 7 years, and produce them to the Ministry for Revenue electronically on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act 2003, exported goods and services supplied to non-residents for consumption wholly outside Samoa are zero-rated. Algorithmic market-making and proprietary HFT execution fees charged to offshore counterparties qualify where the supplier is VAGST-registered, the services are physically performed from Samoa, no Samoan land or goods are involved, and written export evidence is retained. A tax-exempt IC cannot issue 0% invoices or reclaim input VAGST; zero-rating applies only after a valid election to be taxable and VAGST registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or original Air Waybill evidencing physical export (for goods) or executed offshore service contract (for HFT services)
Certificate of Incorporation and proof of IC status from the Samoa International Companies Registry
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment instruction evidencing receipt of foreign currency from the offshore counterparty
VAGST invoice and reconciliation schedule showing the 0% rate applied
Annual return and tax-exempt status confirmation from the Ministry for Revenue where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue audits zero-rated claims under the VAGST Act 2003; fraudulent export zero-rating or false customs declarations attract penalty tax of 150% of the tax evaded, late-payment interest, clawback of any wrongfully refunded VAGST, criminal liability including imprisonment for fraudulent conduct under the Crimes Act 2013, and deregistration of the offending supplier. The Customs Act 2014 separately imposes forfeiture and administrative fines for false export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; the Bank administers the Exchange Control Act 1970 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1971, supervises all licensed commercial banks, and hosts the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) responsible for AML/CFT supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a fixed exchange-rate regime pegged to a trade-weighted basket of currencies comprising the USD, NZD, AUD, EUR, CNY, and JPY. Current-account transactions (goods, services, interest, and dividend payments) are generally convertible through authorized dealer banks upon submission of underlying documentation. Capital-account transactions (direct investment, portfolio flows, loans, and capital repatriation) require prior case-by-case approval from the Central Bank of Samoa. Registered International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 1987 are statutorily exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1970; accordingly, the IC enjoys unrestricted current- and capital-account convertibility, free remittance of profits, dividends, and capital, and full freedom to hold and settle in USD or any foreign currency, subject only to authorized-dealer AML/KYC protocols and CRS/FATCA reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For ordinary resident exporters, the Exchange Control Act 1970 mandates that export proceeds be received within the contracted payment period and in any event no later than three (3) months from the date of shipment or service completion, and that the foreign currency be offered for conversion to an authorized dealer bank as directed by the Central Bank. For the International Company engaged in algorithmic high-frequency trading, proprietary trading revenues constitute exported financial services; however, the statutory exchange-control exemption under the International Companies Act 1987 disapplies all surrender and conversion obligations. The IC may retain and deploy 100% of its USD trading revenues both onshore and offshore without repatriation or conversion mandates, provided the bank records the economic purpose code for statistical reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Samoa has no standalone electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing framework; digital banking and money transmission services require a license under the Financial Institutions Act 1996 (as amended) and full compliance with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie) may serve only as supplementary clearing channels, not as the principal banking relationship, because of transaction-velocity thresholds, restricted prime-broker funding rails, and incompatibility with ultra-low-latency market-making settlement. A Samoa International Company is legally permitted to maintain offshore accounts, provided beneficial-ownership filings under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) remain current and no prohibited business is conducted with Samoa residents.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated for at least one director (or an authorized signatory with a certified board resolution) attending the Apia branch of the tier-1 bank for original-document verification and a face-to-face KYC interview; no fully remote onboarding is permitted for a newly incorporated International Company. The Central Bank of Samoa's customer-due-diligence regime does not allow corporate secretaries, introducers, or notarized bundles to substitute for the initial physical interview. Subsequent signatory changes may be effected remotely through notarized resolutions and SWIFT-tested instruction forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model flagged as algorithmic high-frequency trading with high wire velocity, low human oversight, and no conventional invoice trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Algorithmic trading compliance and risk-management manual; exchange membership and market-making license certificates; third-party technical audit of execution algorithms and automated kill-switch controls; audited financial statements for two prior periods; complete list of prime brokers, exchanges, and omnibus settlement accounts; and a board resolution identifying all expected counterparty flow types.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore holding or trust structure with non-resident beneficial owners and nominee shareholder arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation and current Memorandum and Articles of Association; register of shareholders and directors; beneficial-ownership declaration identifying every 10% or greater beneficial owner (name, nationality, tax residence, TIN); source-of-wealth narrative with supporting brokerage and bank statements; and a legal opinion from Samoa counsel confirming compliance with the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound seed-capital transfers from third-country jurisdictions without corresponding trade commitments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital injection or shareholders' loan agreement; remitter's bank and brokerage statements evidencing lawful accumulation of funds; tax residence certificates and tax identification numbers of all funding parties; sworn source-of-funds affidavit; and pre-funding notification to the receiving bank at least five business days prior to the wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring outbound wires to prime brokers and exchanges settling to third-party omnibus or segregated accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed prime brokerage and exchange connectivity agreements; standing instruction letter listing approved settlement beneficiaries and account numbers; daily FIX/API trade confirmation files reconcilable to each wire; ISO 20022 payment purpose codes (MARG, TRAD, SECU); and quarterly external audit confirmation of treasury settlement operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent shareholder's or investor's bank to the IC's USD Capital Escrow Account at a tier-1 Samoa commercial bank (ANZ or BSP). The remitter must route funds through the receiving bank's USD correspondent (ANZ's or BSP's New York correspondent) and include ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (equity injection) or CAPT (capital payment), with a remittance narrative matching the executed capital injection agreement. The receiving bank verifies the remitter's KYC file before crediting; cleared funds are then released to the Operational Account by internal book transfer upon board-approved treasury mandate. For funding sourced from the IC's own offshore brokerage accounts, purpose code CRED is used and a reconciled statement of the originating brokerage account must be provided.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements and margin disbursements are executed via (i) SWIFT MT103 messages through the tier-1 bank's correspondent network to the prime broker's settlement bank, with final delivery on Fedwire for US-based counterparties; and (ii) direct exchange clearing rails (Direct_Exchange_Clearing), whereby the IC settles direct clearing-house obligations through a clearing membership or sponsored clearing arrangement. For any ancillary physical-commodity cover trades, a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 may be issued through the bank's trade finance desk. All outbound USD wires require pre-funded balances in the Operational Account with no intraday overdraft facilities, a pre-validated beneficiary standing settlement list, and FIX/API trade confirmations archived for a minimum of five years. New settlement instructions must be verified via MT199/MT299 test-key exchange before first use.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (WST/USD) transacted with licensed authorized dealer banks, tenors up to 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the WST, cash-settled in USD with offshore counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between WST and USD for structural hedging of Samoan-dollar operating and compliance costs
Vanilla European-style FX options on WST/USD for downside protection on dividend distributions and capital repatriation
Over-the-counter FX tom-next and spot-next swaps for intraday and overnight liquidity squaring within the settlement window

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before the anniversary of incorporation each year; a 60-day administrative grace period is applied before penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$50 or 10% of the annual fee, whichever is greater; continued non-payment for 90 consecutive days initiates administrative strike-off of the International Company without court action

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement for a standard International Company regardless of share capital, revenue, or trading volume; the company is exempt from audit unless it engages in licensed banking, trust, or insurance business or the Registrar otherwise orders an independent examination
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Samoa International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) requires accounting records to sufficiently reflect transactions and financial position; IFRS may be adopted voluntarily but is not mandated for internal record-keeping

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and verify beneficial ownership particulars on a continuous basis; no public annual UBO confirmation is filed with the Registrar, but any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and the UBO profile updated no later than the following business day; the UBO statement must remain available at the registered office for inspection by the Registrar upon demand

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 - US$1,800 per annum depending on the corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable - no statutory audit required; US$0

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for resident companies; 0% for International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are fully exempt from Samoa income tax on worldwide income. No capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax, and no stamp duty on transfers of IC shares or assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (IC-AR) filed through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IC-AR must be filed within 30 days of the anniversary date of incorporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the International Company as entered in the Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name on the Certificate of Incorporation; no changes without prior approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique IOC registration number assigned by SIFA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain from the Certificate of Incorporation; verify before submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed Samoa registered agent responsible for the IC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent’s details are fixed on the public register; any change must be filed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Street address of the registered office in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical address in Samoa; P.O. Boxes are not sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the prescribed annual government fee has been paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is made through the registered agent; non-resident shareholders do not pay directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the IC carries on a relevant activity and, if so, compliance with the Samoa Economic Substance Regulations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading, declare whether any regulated HFT activity is conducted in Samoa; typically 'No' unless a Samoa trading desk exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of gross revenue and total assets for the financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For exempt ICs, report only Samoa-source revenue; non-Samoa trading gains and assets are included for statistical purposes but are not taxable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a fine of WST 50 per month, up to a maximum of WST 500. Non-payment of the annual government fee may lead to automatic strike-off of the IC, restoration fees, and late payment surcharges imposed by the Samoa International Finance Authority.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies; the International Companies Act exempts distributions to non-resident shareholders from Samoa withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For domestic tax purposes, no DTA relief is required for IC dividend payments. If a distribution were nonetheless classified as taxable by the Samoa Revenue Authority, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, submit it together with Form WHT-1 and the relevant treaty article to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before the remittance date, and provide a written declaration of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 15% for companies taxed under the Income Tax Act 2012. International Companies are statutorily exempt from this withholding tax. Where a treaty applies, typical reduced rates are 10% for royalties and 5-10% for interest, subject to submission of the TRC and treaty claim form.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No transfer pricing documentation threshold is separately prescribed for International Companies. For Samoa resident companies under the Income Tax Act, mandatory Local File and Master File documentation is expected when aggregate related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 per annum.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 and the Economic Substance Regulations require an International Company carrying on a 'relevant activity' to demonstrate economic substance in Samoa, including adequate physical presence, no outsourcing of core income-generating activity, and submission of an annual economic substance declaration. Proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading is in scope if conducted through a Samoa operation; otherwise the IC should record 'no relevant activity' and maintain sufficient evidence to rebut any tax authority challenge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa International Company vehicle to hide income derived from Samoa operations, or misrepresenting the IC as a shell while carrying on active trading with Samoa residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation of the IC as a resident Samoa company and reassessment of 27% corporate income tax plus interest and penalties of up to 100% of the underpaid tax; criminal fine and imprisonment under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise or conceal the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; criminal conviction attracts a term of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false economic substance declaration or maintaining the IC without any physical office, employees, or decision-making records despite carrying on a relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off of the IC and freezing of bank accounts; civil penalty of up to WST 100,000 under the Economic Substance Regulations; failure to remedy within 30 days may lead to loss of tax-exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the penalty if they certified the annual declaration knowing it to be false; may face travel bans and disqualification from corporate management in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence, record beneficial ownership, or report suspicious proceeds derived from algorithmic market manipulation or unauthorised trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to WST 500,000 and monetary penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018; seizure of trading assets and accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are personally criminally liable for culpable AML lapses; cooperation may reduce penalties, but knowledge of suspicious transactions attracts up to 10 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to produce Local File or Master File documentation when the Samoa IC has related-party transactions exceeding the threshold, or mispricing algorithmic trading execution and clearing fees to erode taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of taxable income to an arm's length level, imposition of a 20% adjustment penalty, and interest on the resulting underpayment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate transfer pricing disclosures may be personally liable for penalties in their capacity as preparers of tax returns; immunity applies only upon demonstrating reasonable care.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Prohibited Trading and Capital Repatriation Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting proprietary high-frequency trading on behalf of Samoa residents without a statutory trading licence, or repatriating profits disguised as loans or management fees to circumvent exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the IC's tax-exempt status, imposition of 27% corporate income tax on all income derived from Samoa, and penalty equal to 100% of the tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil when the IC is used for fraud or evasion; directors are personally liable for restitution, may be subject to international travel bans, and can be extradited to Samoa for criminal prosecution.
